articles.title: Sanju Samson's blitz against Afghanistan keeps Vaibhav Sooryavanshi waiting - and the debate alive
articles.summary: Cricket News: New Delhi: Mohammad Nabi moved to his left, leaped ever so slightly at the long-off boundary rope, got his hands underneath the leather and held on. A.
articles.body: New Delhi: Mohammad Nabi moved to his left, leaped ever so slightly at the long-off boundary rope, got his hands underneath the leather and held on. A few inches more and the ball would have possibly evaded him for a six. Instead, he gestured 'out' to the umpire and a probing Rashid Khan. The Afghanistan spinner checked if the foot was planted safely and comfortably inside the field of play. The moment he got the nod, the 27-year-old went on to celebrate his second wicket of the over. Sanju Samson walked back after scoring 57 runs from 22 balls, hitting seven fours and four sixes along the way.As far as rubber stamping their places go, this was Samson's attempt - with 52 of his 57 runs coming in boundaries. In a game of musical chairs that he's been involved in with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Samson has, arguably, had the raw end of the deal. And here he was, suggesting once again that he wasn't going away easily.On the back of a stellar T20 World Cup, playing a huge role in India winning the trophy, he was benched unceremoniously after a poor showing against Ireland. In came Sooryavanshi, who didn't hit the ground running on his inauguration to the international stage. Samson then returned for the last two T20I against England before missing the flight to Zimbabwe. There, Sooryavanshi who went hammer and tongs and emerged as the Player of the Match.Yet, as the T20I series against Afghanistan rolled around, Samson was picked to open the innings alongside Abhishek Sharma. He started the series with just 10 before producing the goods in the second contest.Azmatullah Omarzai and Mohammad Nabi bore the bulk of his prolific shot-making at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on Tuesday. The former conceded 23 from 10 balls while the latter went for 22 from seven deliveries. The aspect that stood out, and stands out in most Samson knocks, is the ease with which he clear the in-field.An overpitched start to the fifth over by Omarzai was sent over the mid-on fielder. Next ball, short and spraying down leg side, he sent it over the fine leg region. The one after that was pitched up and again met the treatment: slashed over the cover, one bounce and it went into the hands of the volunteers. To end the over, Samson converted a low full toss with the full face of his bat, knocked over the stumps at the non-striker's end and yet beat the fielder for a four!Even Rashid Khan was whacked for a four and a six before the Afghanistan spinner, and rest of the bowlers, perhaps, breathed a collective sigh of relief."It’s about just watching the ball and trying to get maximum out in the powerplay. Sometimes it works out well, sometimes it doesn’t. After a few failures, you definitely go through a lot. Being an Indian cricketer, it’s not easy to face failures, but that’s where my experience comes in," he said in the post-match press conference."I try to shut out the noise, try to be confident and come out and still keep scoring at a high strike rate, even taking the chances, even knowing that if I fail again, I will be facing a lot of noise. But I think that’s the way we are built here in Indian cricket. I just go out there and try to score maximum and contribute," he continued.As Samson took the crease in the first T20I, and not Sooryavanshi, the experts were divided. Kris Srikanth argued that Sooryavanshi "wasn't being treated properly". R Ashwin, meanwhile, implored the selectors, coaches and beyond to "understand his position." And yet, Samson gets how challenging making this call between the two is."It’s a very challenging place to be in. Right from the whole team management, the captain, coach and selectors. It’s a very tough choice, actually. All of them (himself, Sooryavanshi and Abhishek Sharma) are really good, all of them are performing, and all of them have to be given the right opportunity to keep performing at the international level," said Samson."It’s a very tough decision. I totally understand. I lead an IPL franchise, so I know how hard these decisions are, and everyone has been performing really well.""I have been in this kind of space for quite a few years, so I just know how to balance it out. Just think about what is in my control and try to be very positive with your competitors as well."I think they are competitors for the outside world, but we are a team and we are playing for a country. We want to win the game first, and then it comes down to the other individuals."We try to be as positive as possible, and whoever is playing, we want them to do well. We just have to be ready for our own opportunity. We can’t sulk or be in a negative frame of mind, thinking, 'Yaar, mujhe nahi mila, usko kyun diya?' Those kinds of mindsets don’t work here," he explained.For now, Samson has seemingly stalled the debate with a cracking knock in New Delhi. But whether it is enough to get a longer rope, with continued chances, remains to be seen.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: On 26th b’day, Saudi Arabia-based YouTuber pays for followers’ feast
articles.summary: YouTuber Anurag Dwivedi marks 26th birthday with free meals in Unnao-Nawabganj as ED probes alleged betting-linked money laundering and asset seizures.
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Almost a year after the Enforcement Directorate registered a case against Saudi Arabia-based YouTuber Anurag Dwivedi and seized property in his hometown of Unnao, claiming it was amassed through unlawful means, the social media influencer celebrated his 26th birthday on Sunday in style.Dwivedi asked his followers to visit select eateries in Unnao and Nawabganj, enjoy a meal in his name and leave the bill to him.Describing it as a birthday celebration, he thanked his followers for their support. The cricket content creator has more than seven million YouTube subscribers and 2.4 million Instagram followers.Dwivedi posted a video on social media from Saudi Arabia around 12.30 pm, announcing that anyone could walk into several eateries in Unnao and eat for free.His message was simple: “Eat in my name, I’ll pay the bill.”The announcement quickly drew crowds at some of the participating outlets in Unnao and Nawabganj, with people queuing up to avail themselves of the offer.He named a few food outlets where people could enjoy dosa, ‘chhole-bhature’, samosa or pizza.Beginning his video with religious slogans, Dwivedi said he had turned 26 and wanted to celebrate not only with people in Nawabganj and Unnao but with people across the country.He said that even travellers on the Lucknow-Kanpur highway could take advantage of the offer at participating outlets.Towards the end of the video, he said completing 26 years in ‘Kalyug’ was itself a major achievement. He thanked his followers, expressed his affection for them and signed off with ‘Love you’ and ‘Jai Mata Ki’. The video was shared by his relatives and friends on social media.A resident of Nawabganj, around 27 km from the Unnao district headquarters, Dwivedi has built a substantial social media following. His online content largely revolves around cricket and cricketers, and he has also been associated with the online fantasy sports and gaming ecosystem.He made headlines last year after marrying his Lucknow-based girlfriend aboard a cruise in Dubai on Nov 22, 2025.The ED’s money laundering case against Dwivedi stems from a 2022 online betting racket busted in Siliguri, West Bengal.Five alleged supervisors of a betting syndicate operating through Telegram channels and platforms such as Skyexchange were arrested, and investigators identified Badal Bhardwaj as the alleged mastermind.As investigators tracked the money trail, they found transactions linked to accounts held by Dwivedi’s relatives and associates, prompting the ED to initiate a money laundering probe.The agency alleges that proceeds from illegal betting apps were routed through mule accounts and hawala networks into companies and family accounts linked to Dwivedi without any legitimate business basis.The probe led to searches across Lucknow, Unnao, Delhi, Mumbai, Surat and Varanasi in late 2025 and early 2026.During the raids, the ED seized luxury vehicles, including a Lamborghini Urus, Mercedes, BMW Z4, Ford Endeavour and Mahindra Thar, recovered around Rs 20 lakh in cash, and froze bank deposits, insurance policies and other assets.Officials also claimed to have found evidence of hawala transactions and investments in Dubai real estate.ED froze or attached assets worth between Rs 20 crore and Rs 23.7 crore. articles.title: Sunil Gavaskar urges BCCI to make big change, names Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid for key role
articles.summary: Cricket News: Sunil Gavaskar believes the BCCI needs to rethink the role of its Cricket Advisory Committee (CAC), suggesting that the panel should have a far wider .
articles.body: Sunil Gavaskar believes the BCCI needs to rethink the role of its Cricket Advisory Committee (CAC), suggesting that the panel should have a far wider mandate and draw on the experience of some of India's most celebrated former cricketers.The former India captain's call comes after he criticised East Zone's approach in the Duleep Trophy final, where Ishan Kishan's side settled for the title on the basis of a first-innings lead. Gavaskar has previously expressed his dissatisfaction with the rule, which has continued to attract criticism over several domestic seasons.According to Gavaskar, the CAC could play a much larger role in addressing such issues and shaping the future of Indian cricket.Gavaskar wants bigger role for CACThe current CAC appointments date back to 2022, when Ashok Malhotra, Jatin Paranjape and Sulakshana Naik were named to the three-member panel. Its traditional responsibilities have centred on selecting the head coach and national selectors, with the committee also conducting interviews for those positions.However, there is uncertainty over whether the CAC still exists in its current form or has been disbanded.Gavaskar believes the BCCI should instead broaden the committee's remit to cover wider aspects of the game, including domestic and international scheduling."There are no longer any committees in BCCI today apart from the selection committees and the CAC. Perhaps the time has come to expand the CAC and its brief of selecting the selectors and coach, and also look at fixtures — domestic and international, and all things related to Indian cricket. There are some incredibly experienced former cricketers whose expertise can be utilised to be on this committee," Gavaskar wrote in his column for the Mid-Day.He also suggested a star-studded list of former India players who could contribute to such a panel."How about names like Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid, Sourav Ganguly, Ravi Shastri, Anil Kumble, Harbhajan Singh, Virender Sehwag — to name a few? The President and Secretary will be there too," he added.'It carries a heft beyond measure'Gavaskar believes involving former greats such as Tendulkar and Dravid in discussions with India's coaching and development setup could bring an additional level of expertise and authority."When this committee interacts with the coach and captain and the head of the NCA, it carries a heft beyond measure. A similar committee for women’s cricket, too, where experience and expertise meet to take calls to take Indian cricket forward," wrote Gavaskar.The former batter, who also captained India to the 1985 Championship win, wants the idea to extend beyond the men's game, with a comparable advisory structure for women's cricket."Just thinking about this gives one the goosebumps. Will it ever happen, or is it just a dream?" he concluded.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'He thought I was joking': Brendon McCullum reveals dramatic phone call that brought Kevin Pietersen back
articles.summary: Cricket News: Kevin Pietersen's return to the England setup has Brendon McCullum at the centre of the decision, with the white-ball head coach revealing that the id.
articles.body: Kevin Pietersen's return to the England setup has Brendon McCullum at the centre of the decision, with the white-ball head coach revealing that the idea of bringing the former England batter in as a mentor was his own.The England and Wales Cricket Board confirmed last week that Pietersen would join the coaching group for the ODI and T20I assignments leading up to the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe.Pietersen's appointment immediately raised eyebrows given his outspoken criticism of McCullum and England's preparations in the past. In 2025, he questioned the team's readiness for the ODI series against India ahead of the Champions Trophy and was particularly critical of the way the side had approached the assignment.But McCullum insists there is no lingering tension between the pair. Speaking ahead of England's first T20I against Sri Lanka on Monday, he explained that Pietersen's previous criticism was never a barrier to bringing him into the setup.'I have no problem with that'McCullum said he directly approached Pietersen about the role and was initially met with disbelief.“When I rang him the first time, I said, ‘Would you be interested in coming to work with England?’ He thought I was joking for a start. And then he sort of mentioned, I've been quite critical of you guys in the past. I said, I have no problem with that, mate. There are parts of it I agree with, and there are parts I won't agree with. And that's fine. That's what the beauty of Kev coming in. He's obviously got an incredible pedigree as a player. A lot of our guys grew up watching and idolising Kev when he was in his pomp as a player as well,” McCullum told reporters on Monday ahead of the 1st T20I against Sri Lanka.Pietersen has already made an impression since joining the group, according to McCullum. Rather than restricting his contribution to a particular area, the England coach wants the former batter to assess the wider environment and challenge existing thinking.“He's brought a ton of energy to the setup within the last 24 hours already. I've mentioned to him that I don't want him to just try and be buried in one specific skill set either. I want him to look across the environment and setup, and challenge me privately on ways we can improve or thingswe can do differently. Our relationship is good,” he added.McCullum confirms Pietersen was his ideaMcCullum also stressed that their relationship is built on mutual respect, despite their contrasting views in the past.“It's full of respect. We play against each other and we've enjoyed spending the time together over the last little while or two. I'm super excited to have him. I know he's super excited to be here. The boys are buzzing, and I'm pleased that we can add such a strong resource to what's already a very, very strong coaching staff of mine,” said McCullum.When asked directly whether Pietersen's appointment had originated with him, McCullum gave a straightforward answer.“Yeah, it was my idea.”For McCullum, Pietersen's willingness to commit fully to a task and his ability to offer an alternative perspective are among the qualities that make him valuable to the England setup.“Hs work ethic is obviously second to none as well right throughout his career. When he's in on something, he's all in as well. I also think sometimes having someone who has a different take on things is no bad thing,” said McCullum.Pietersen is also familiar with the mentor's role, having previously worked in a similar capacity with Delhi Capitals in the Indian Premier League. Now, his experience will be available to England across the white-ball campaign leading into the World Cup.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mohsin Naqvi set to take drastic steps; Aaqib Javed, Wahab Riaz could face axe
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan cricket could be heading for another major overhaul, with PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi reportedly preparing sweeping changes following the Test .
articles.body: Pakistan cricket could be heading for another major overhaul, with PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi reportedly preparing sweeping changes following the Test team’s disastrous tour of England.Pakistan were beaten 0-3 in the Test series in England, a result that pushed them down to ninth in the ICC rankings. The poor run has already triggered significant changes, including the removal of two coaches and a major reshuffle of the playing squad.Now, according to a PTI report, the Pakistan Cricket Board is considering changes to the national selection committee, with former Test cricketer Aaqib Javed among those who could be removed from his role as senior selector.Aaqib Javed could be next to goA PCB source indicated that Naqvi has recognised the need for drastic action after the continued instability surrounding the national side."Even Mohsin Naqvi has now realised that some radical measures are required to end the losing streak and abrupt happenings in Pakistan cricket. So these changes are now on the cards," an internal source said.Javed was at the centre of the controversial changes made to Pakistan’s Test squad earlier this month, shortly after the team lost the Lord’s Test against England.Seven players were sent home following that defeat, while head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul were also released from their duties. Javed has also faced criticism previously over frequent changes to Pakistan’s coaching staff and captaincy.The possible shake-up could extend beyond the men’s selection committee.Wahab Riaz, another former Pakistan bowler who is currently working as a mentor with the women’s team, is also expected to be released from his duties after the Asian Games campaign in Japan later this month.The PCB’s decision to make changes to the coaching setup during the England tour was also linked to Mike Hesson’s growing interest in taking charge of the men’s team across all formats.The New Zealand coach is currently Pakistan’s white-ball coach, but sources said he has shown keen interest in taking up the all-format role.At the same time, the PCB has been in talks with several foreign coaches over the vacant head coach position with the women’s team following the Asian Games."Naqvi will soon hold a high-level meeting with his aides and also take the governing board members into confidence before final decisions are made on the changes," the source said.Hesson wants clarity before taking red-ball roleHesson, however, is understood to have made his expectations clear before agreeing to take charge of Pakistan’s red-ball setup.He has said he needs sufficient time to get the system in motion and wants a confirmed timeframe for the assignment. Hesson has also sought assurances that he will have freedom from interference in his decision-making.With Naqvi now preparing to consult his aides and the PCB governing board, Pakistan cricket could be in line for another round of significant changes in the coming days.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Kevin Pietersen: Why England mentor will bring unfiltered challenge Brendon McCullum needs - Finn
articles.summary: Kevin Pietersen can be blunt and forthright and there is no better time than now to add that challenge to England's white-ball set-up, says Steven Finn.
articles.body:
I was as surprised as most that Kevin Pietersen has joined the England coaching ranks as a mentor in the build-up to the 50-over World Cup in South Africa next autumn.

Not only was his last interaction with the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) sitting in the offices at Lord's being told he wouldn't play for England again in 2014, but the success of his YouTube channel, The Switch, and the time it takes to commit to something like that made it seem inconceivable that it could work.

However, when I took a step back to remember what it was like to share a dressing room with him at the beginning of my England career, I remembered a number of occasions that lead me to believe this can only be a good thing for all parties.

Kevin can be blunt and forthright, but dressing rooms need that in order to function properly. They can't be an echo chamber.

On the white-ball tour of India last year, while working for the host broadcaster, he was bemoaning the lack of practice , external that England's players had opted for in the build-up to games.

His practice was always intense and with purpose. Usually, he would come up to me as he was walking into the net and say he was going to smash me everywhere and not get out. That would usually rile me up to try to bowl quicker in order to not let him have it his way.

He wanted to make sure the practice had that bit more on it, something that is important when steeling your mind and reactions to go out and play at the highest level.

I used to enjoy the battles in the nets and it made me a better bowler by having competitive nets against one of the best players in the world.

We'd constantly be arguing about what angle the fielders were when he was deciding how many runs he'd scored off that ball, or whether I thought it could have gone to hand when he hit it in the air.

Follow ball-by-ball commentary on BBC Sounds, BBC Radio 5 Sports and the BBC Sport website and app. Live text updates and in-play video clips on the website and app. Extended highlights on BBC Two and BBC iPlayer from 23:05 BST.

Kev was ahead of his time with both his mindset and skills. The inventor of the switch hit, and the most ardent supporter of the IPL before it became mainstream.

The flamingo flicks through mid-wicket in Test matches and hitting Glenn McGrath back over his head for six at Lord's in 2005.

None of which would look out of place now in 2026.

But, he never thought he'd cracked the game.

In 2012 when we were in Sri Lanka, I remember turning up for training at the SSC in Colombo to play a warm-up game and Kev had already been there for an hour facing local left-arm spin bowlers in order to try to correct his technique ( ironically overseen by Andy Flower ) that had been a problem for him intermittently.

As a result of that hard work he scored the most remarkable 151 against Rangana Herath in the second Test, hitting him to all parts, and backed it up later that year against India away to seal a historic red-ball series victory where his runs, particularly in Mumbai, formed the bedrock of the win.

Those runs and the manner with which they were scored, wouldn't have been possible without those long practice sessions while people weren't watching.

It wasn't just about him improving too. In Perth during the 2013-14 Ashes, when Mitchell Johnson and his moustache were running amok, it wouldn't be out of place to see a tailender looking shellshocked at the prospect of having to go and face him in the corner of the dressing room.

I vividly remember KP coming over to me (even though I wasn't in the starting XI), and saying 'let's go practice facing the short ball in the nets'. He threw bouncers at my head and helped me figure out a technique to be able to play (mainly evade) the short-pitched bowling.

I don't know whether at that stage of the tour he just wanted to be out of the dressing room rather than in it, but it helped me.

I can see him doing similar things with players he sees areas of improvement with in his role as mentor.

Kevin was never shy of letting the dressing room know his thoughts when debriefing a match, or when discussing the team's approach.

I saw this first hand with his dissent towards a fitness fielding session in the build-up to the 2014 Sydney Test match, among others.

Some may argue that bringing this into an environment that is clearly working and improving may be a bad thing.

However, I believe McCullum has learned from the way the Test team turned a corner as soon as everything seemed in order.

Pietersen comes from an era where there was no substitute for hard work and your main way of making a decent living from the game was by playing Test cricket - where you needed to work hard on a fundamental technique in order to firstly survive, but then to build and expand upon to be good at other formats.

The balance has clearly shifted now and the power lies with the players able to globetrot and play franchise tournaments.

In my eyes the 50-over format is now closer to the pace of modern Test cricket than T20 cricket, helping players with the fundamentals, married up with a strong work ethic can only be a good thing when looking to excel in the format, especially in conditions where there will be passages where the bowlers may be on top.

But, I believe he will bring this attitude to the dressing room for the next 14 months leading up to that World Cup.

There is no better time to introduce a voice of challenge than now, as it means that the team will not be able to simply maraud on as they have been without checks and balances.

Pietersen will provide this, unfiltered.

articles.title: England mentor Kevin Pietersen asked to 'challenge' coach Brendon McCullum
articles.summary: Cricket News: England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum has asked newly appointed mentor Kevin Pietersen to challenge the team’s setup and speak up with ideas .
articles.body: England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum has asked newly appointed mentor Kevin Pietersen to challenge the team’s setup and speak up with ideas that could help improve the side.Pietersen was appointed last week and joined England’s coaching staff ahead of the T20 series against Sri Lanka. His role will continue through a busy period that includes next year's one-day international World Cup."He's obviously got an incredible pedigree as a player and a lot of guys grew up idolising Kev. He's brought a ton of energy to the setup within the last 24 hours," McCullum told reporters on Monday.McCullum said he did not want Pietersen to focus on one particular area and instead encouraged him to look at the wider setup and question the team's methods."I've mentioned to him that I don't want him to be buried in one specific skillset. I want him to look across the environment and challenge me privately around ways we can improve or things we can do differently."McCullum was sacked as England's Test coach in July, with his tenure affected by off-field controversies involving players including Ben Stokes, Harry Brook and Gus Atkinson.Fast bowler Brydon Carse was then left out of England's Test squad during their recent 3-0 series win over Pakistan following an incident outside a nightclub.McCullum has now said players will have to maintain professional standards if they want to be selected for England."There is a lot of talent around - if you're not prepared to do that, there are other guys who will be given those opportunities," he added."As far as Carsey is concerned, it's important for Carsey he gets his house in order. articles.body: Australia captain Pat Cummins expects the Test team could encounter some hostility when it returns to South Africa for its first red-ball tour there since the infamous Sandpaper Gate scandal of 2018.Australia are scheduled to play three ODIs and three Tests in South Africa. Although the Australians have continued to visit the country for white-ball cricket since the ball-tampering controversy, the upcoming Test series will mark their first in South Africa since the incident.Cummins is currently not with Australia for the three-match ODI series in Zimbabwe but will link up with the squad in South Africa for the one-dayers before the Test campaign begins on October 9.Cummins expects some hostility in South AfricaSpeaking on the Keepin’ it Cricket podcast, Cummins acknowledged that the 2018 episode could still be brought up by sections of the home support."There might be a little bit of hostility," Cummins admitted. "(But) it can't be louder than an Ashes series … Birmingham, the Hollies Stand at Edgbaston, that gets pretty rowdy."The Australian skipper has already experienced South African crowds during previous white-ball tours and was also one of the standout performers during Australia's 2018 Test series against the Proteas.He does not expect anything completely unfamiliar when Australia return for the three-Test contest."As long as I've been to South Africa, there are some parts of the crowd that get stuck in, but I reckon we've seen it all before."And most importantly, I'm captain, so I'm in the middle; I'm not near the fence!"'Everyone moves on', says Australian captainCummins also suggested that the reaction to Sandpaper Gate may not be as intense as some might expect. He recalled that the issue had been heavily discussed during previous encounters but felt the response from South African fans was ultimately less dramatic than anticipated."It (Sandpapergate) was kind of really spoken up (in past series), and it was almost a bit underwhelming," Cummins said about the reaction from Proteas fans.For Cummins, the best way to move beyond the controversy will be to focus on the cricket once the series gets underway."Everyone moves on. The good thing is, three Tests, you get stuck into the cricket, and everyone just worries about the cricket pretty quickly."I'm sure there'll be some rowdy people in the crowd, and some articles or some media bring up stuff. But our group's moved on," he added.Australia still have six players in their current setup who were part of the squad that lost the 2018 series 1-3 to South Africa. The tour became one of the darkest episodes in Australian cricket after the ball-tampering scandal led to year-long bans for Steve Smith and David Warner, while Cameron Bancroft was suspended for nine months.Cummins rejects preparation excuse after Bangladesh lossCummins also reflected on Australia's recent defeat to Bangladesh in Darwin, their first home loss to the Bangla Tigers.The result prompted questions over whether Australia had been adequately prepared for the series, but Cummins dismissed that suggestion."Whether that was an Ashes Test or a Bangladesh series, I think we would have prepped exactly the same. Of course you look at it after the series, but I actually thought we were in a really good spot; everyone fit, firing."The Australian captain accepted, however, that his side simply failed to perform at the required level in Darwin."I just don’t think we played very well. I don’t think it was a lack of prep. I just don’t think we were at our best, and Bangladesh played brilliantly, and didn’t really let us in," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Greg Chappell leads seven Australia captains in appeal to foreign minister over 'humanitarian' Imran Khan concerns
articles.summary: Cricket News: Mumbai: Former Australia captain and India head coach Greg Chappell has stepped up his efforts to secure fair medical treatment and welfare for former.
articles.body: Mumbai: Former Australia captain and India head coach Greg Chappell has stepped up his efforts to secure fair medical treatment and welfare for former Pakistan Prime Minister and 1992 World Cup-winning captain Imran Khan.As part of Chappell's latest initiative, seven former Australia captains have approached Foreign Minister Penny Wong over humanitarian concerns surrounding Imran's detention in Pakistan. They have urged the Australian Government to raise the matter directly with the relevant Pakistani authorities.The letter, a copy of which is with TOI, was signed by Allan Border, Greg Chappell, Ian Chappell, Belinda Clark, Kim Hughes, Mark Taylor and Steve Waugh. They stressed that they were writing "not as diplomats or political actors, but as former Australian captains who felt we should speak up."The group said it was taking no position on the legal or political case against Imran, which it described as a matter for Pakistan. Their concern, they said, was the treatment of anyone in detention, calling it “a matter of basic humanity, whatever their politics.”The former captains highlighted concerns raised publicly by Imran's sons and sisters over his health and treatment, including limited medical care, restricted family contact and minimal access to legal counsel.The letter also referred to Chappell's last meeting with Imran in Islamabad in 2022, when he was Pakistan's prime minister and, according to Chappell, "hale, hearty and fit.""Greg Chappell last saw Imran Khan in Islamabad in 2022, when Khan was Prime Minister — hale, hearty and fit, by his account. It is hard to reconcile that image with the reports now coming out of his detention, and that is why we write to you today, not as diplomats or political actors, but as former Australian captains who felt we should speak up. Khan led Pakistan to its only World Cup title. He also led his country as Prime Minister. Australians hold him in great regard — as a cricketer whose skill and leadership left a lasting mark on the game we share, and as someone who has helped improve the lives of Pakistanis by building cancer hospitals.""Beyond credible reports, his own sons and sisters have been pleading publicly for months over his health and treatment in detention — limited medical care, restricted family contact, and minimal access to legal counsel among their concerns."The letter concluded: "This is not the first time international captains have raised this concern. It has been brought to public attention on two separate occasions in the past six months, and the reports since then — now echoed by his own family — suggest the situation has not improved. We would be grateful if the Australian Government could raise this directly with the relevant Pakistani authorities. Mr Chappell has also requested a meeting with you on this matter over recent weeks, and would welcome the chance to discuss it with you directly on our behalf. Thank you for taking the time to consider this."The appeal comes weeks after 21 former international captains from nine cricketing nations, including India's Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev and Dilip Vengsarkar, wrote to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Aug 23 over Imran's medical treatment and welfare.That letter, a follow-up to one signed by 14 former captains in February, followed developments that the group said fell short of a Supreme Court directive on Imran's treatment. The court had ordered that Khan be transferred to hospital for examination by a medical board including his own physicians and his sister, Dr Uzma Khan, alongside reinstated weekly family visits.The 73-year-old Imran has been in jail for more than three years following his tenure as Pakistan's prime minister and is currently facing severe health issues.Since the first letter, Imran's former Pakistan teammates, including a tearful Javed Miandad, Wasim Akram and Moin Khan, have spoken out, as has current Australia captain Pat Cummins.Chappell had also requested a meeting with Wong last month to discuss the matter on behalf of the group but has yet to receive a response.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'This was my last World Cup': Bhuvneshwar Kumar reveals why India return hopes faded
articles.summary: Cricket News: Bhuvneshwar Kumar has once again found himself at the centre of conversations around the Indian team after two impressive IPL seasons with Royal Chall.
articles.body: Bhuvneshwar Kumar has once again found himself at the centre of conversations around the Indian team after two impressive IPL seasons with Royal Challengers Bengaluru.The veteran pacer has not played for India since November 2022, but his performances in RCB's back-to-back IPL title-winning campaigns have revived calls for his return. Bhuvneshwar took 17 wickets in IPL 2025 before producing an even better campaign in 2026, claiming 28 wickets at an average of 17.89. He finished just one wicket short of winning the Purple Cap for a record third time.The 36-year-old has repeatedly played down expectations of an India recall. However, speaking to Jatin Sapru on his YouTube channel, Bhuvneshwar admitted that he feels he deserves another opportunity in the national team."Of course," he told Sapru.But the pacer immediately stressed that an India comeback is not the sole motivation behind his cricket."I'm not playing to prove anything, but I'd be happy to play for India again."Bhuvneshwar no longer waits for India callBhuvneshwar, who last represented India in the T20I series in New Zealand in November 2022, said he has reached a stage where another omission would no longer affect him."I have gone past that time when I used to wait for the next series," he said.After the New Zealand tour, the pacer initially believed the selectors could bring him back into the side. He had received a call from the team management and interpreted it as a possible indication that he would be considered for the following two series.That expectation, however, did not materialise."Till a few series," he said when asked if he expected to return to the Indian side after the New Zealand tour. "Because I had received a call. What they said, based on that I felt maybe next two series. But then I realised it's not what they said."It wasn't hurtful, because then I knew what was happening, and I made peace with it. It wasn't easy, but family played a big role," he added.Bhuvneshwar knew 2022 World Cup could be his lastBhuvneshwar also revealed that he had already sensed his India World Cup career could be over after the team's semifinal defeat to England in Adelaide at the 2022 T20 World Cup.After returning to his room following the loss, he called his wife Nupur and told her that he believed it had been his final World Cup for India."In Adelaide it happened. I came to my room and told my wife. I told this from my experience. In the dressing room, everyone was disappointed. There were a few briefs before we left. But when I came back to my room I told Nupur this was my last World Cup. Because what I have seen from my experience, when you lose a tournament like this selectors want to look ahead, and that is fair," he said.Bhuvneshwar's last India appearance came in Napier in November 2022, shortly after the team's semifinal exit from the T20 World Cup in Australia. While he had initially hoped for another chance, he eventually accepted that the selectors were looking towards the next cycle.His recent IPL form, though, has once again put his name into the conversation around India's T20I setup.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sachin Tendulkar's ODI record broken: Zimbabwe's Brendan Taylor makes history vs Australia
articles.summary: Cricket News: Zimbabwe veteran Brendan Taylor has gone past Sachin Tendulkar to become the longest-serving player in men's ODI history after taking the field in the.
articles.body: Zimbabwe veteran Brendan Taylor has gone past Sachin Tendulkar to become the longest-serving player in men's ODI history after taking the field in the first ODI against Australia in Harare on Tuesday.Taylor's ODI career now spans 22 years and four months, moving him ahead of Tendulkar, whose ODI career lasted 22 years and three months before he retired from the format in 2012.Tendulkar, however, still holds the record for the most ODI runs with 18,426 and the most appearances in the format with 463 matches.Taylor, 40, made his ODI debut in 2004 and has gone on to become one of Zimbabwe's leading batters. Going into Tuesday's match, he had scored a national-record 11 ODI centuries in 207 matches.Taylor retired from international cricket in 2021, but in 2022 he was handed a three-and-a-half-year ban for breaching the ICC's Anti-Corruption and Anti-Doping codes.After completing his suspension, he came out of retirement in 2025 as Zimbabwe began preparing to co-host the 2027 ODI World Cup with South Africa and Namibia.Meanwhile, Australia won the toss on Tuesday and decided to bat in their first one-day cricket international in Zimbabwe in 12 years.Australian captain Mitchell Marsh is one of the three survivors in both teams to have played in the last ODI in Zimbabwe which the host team won. Zimbabwe skipper Sikandar Raza and Brendan Taylor are the other two players, who did compete in that famous Zimbabwe victory in 2014.Lineups:Australia: Mitchell Marsh (captain), Travis Head, Cooper Connolly, Josh Inglis, Alex Carey, Matt Renshaw, Ollie Peake, Xavier Bartlett, Nathan Ellis, Adam Zampa, Spencer Johnson.Zimbabwe: Brian Bennett, Ben Curran, Innocent Kaia, Brendan Taylor, Craig Ervine, Sikandar Raza (captain), Wessly Madhevere, Brad Evans, Newman Nyamhuri, Wellington Masakadza, Blessing Muzarabani.FOLLOW LIVE UPDATESGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ICC Women's T20I Rankings: Shree Charani creates history, becomes first Indian to cross 800-point mark
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Indian players have made big gains in the latest ICC Women’s T20I Player Rankings after India won a record eighth Women’s Asia Cup title.Sh.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian players have made big gains in the latest ICC Women’s T20I Player Rankings after India won a record eighth Women’s Asia Cup title.Shree Charani has strengthened her position at the top of the bowling rankings, while Shafali Verma has moved back into the top six among batters.Charani crosses 800-point markCharani played a key role in India’s Asia Cup final win over Sri Lanka, taking four wickets for 20 runs at the Dubai International Stadium. The left-arm spinner has crossed the 800-point mark for the first time and reached a career-best 804 rating points.It is the highest rating points achieved by an Indian in the ICC Women’s T20I Player Rankings in both batting and bowling.Charani has gone past Mithali Raj’s previous record of 780 points in the batting rankings, which she achieved in 2011. She is now just two points away from the highest rating ever achieved by a women’s T20I bowler.Australia’s Megan Schutt holds the record with 806 points, which she reached in November 2018.Deepti moves up to secondDeepti Sharma has also made a big jump in the bowling rankings. The India all-rounder has moved up four places to second after finishing the Asia Cup as the tournament’s leading wicket-taker with 14 wickets.Seamer Nandani Sharma has climbed 10 places to 94th after an impressive tournament. She was also among the most economical bowlers, giving away only 4.64 runs per over.Leg-spinner Prema Rawat has made an even bigger jump. She has moved up 50 places to 96th.Shafali back in top sixShafali Verma has also made progress in the T20I batting rankings. She has moved up from seventh to sixth after finishing as the Asia Cup’s leading run-scorer with 236 runs.Shafali scored 64 in the semi-final and 68 in the final. Her performances have taken her to 741 rating points, her highest since October 2021. She is now just one place and four points behind teammate Smriti Mandhana. Mandhana is fifth with 745 points after scoring 213 runs in five innings.Shafali has also moved up five places to 15th in the all-rounders’ rankings. She has reached a career-best 221 rating points.Sri Lanka players make progressSri Lanka’s Nilakshika Silva has moved up one place to 44th in the batting rankings. She was the third-highest run-scorer at the Asia Cup with 108 runs.Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu has also moved up one place to 27th in the bowling rankings. Her seven-wicket haul for five runs against Indonesia helped her finish the tournament with 12 wickets. She has retained third place in the all-rounders’ rankings.Bosch makes huge jumpSouth Africa’s ongoing T20I series against Zimbabwe has also led to a major change in the batting rankings. Anneke Bosch has jumped 323 places to 54th after playing a key role in South Africa’s 2-0 lead in the five-match series in Bulawayo.Bosch scored 83 off 43 balls in the first match and followed it with 65 off 31 balls in the second. Her two impressive performances have made her one of the biggest movers in this week’s rankings.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Great source of happiness': Joe Root’s words leave Pakistan’s Razaullah delighted after fearless Edgbaston show
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan’s rising pacer Razaullah has revealed details of a special meeting with England batting great Joe Root after his impressive Test debut at Edg.
articles.body: Pakistan’s rising pacer Razaullah has revealed details of a special meeting with England batting great Joe Root after his impressive Test debut at Edgbaston, where he emerged as one of the few bright spots in Pakistan’s eight-wicket defeat.Joe Root’s words bring joy for RazaullahRazaullah said Root personally met him after the Test and offered valuable advice following his eye-catching performance. The young Pakistan cricketer admitted that receiving praise from a player of Root’s stature was a memorable moment.“Receiving such appreciation from a world-class player was a great source of happiness and encouragement for me,” Razaullah said, as quoted by Pakistan Observer.The interaction capped a remarkable few days for the uncapped pacer, who had been handed a Test debut after the Pakistan Cricket Board made sweeping changes to the squad ahead of the series finale.From emergency call-up to Test heroicsRazaullah was among seven players called up after the PCB released a group of players and coaches, including Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul, before the third Test. With only eight first-class appearances under his belt, the youngster had little experience at the highest level. Yet, he immediately showed why Pakistan had turned to him during a difficult period.The right-arm speedster made an impact with both ball and bat, claiming four wickets before producing a sensational counter-attacking innings that gave Pakistan hope of mounting an unlikely fightback.Nine sixes put Razaullah in record booksPakistan’s position looked desperate after they were dismissed for 133 and England piled up 453. Things became even worse when Pakistan slipped to 0/2 in their second innings. However, Azan Awais, Shan Masood and Babar Azam helped steady the innings before Razaullah took centre stage.The debutant smashed 81 from just 63 deliveries, striking four fours and nine sixes. His nine maximums equalled the record for most sixes by a batter on Test debut, matching New Zealand great Tim Southee.Rather than being intimidated by England’s attack, Razaullah embraced the challenge and took the game to the bowlers.“I was being selective with which balls to slog, but they all seemed within range,” Razaullah said.“I wanted to take it as deep as possible. I wasn't scared of pace. I wanted to punish the balls from Archer that landed on a hard length. There's nothing to be scared of when you're playing for your country. I was just enjoying myself.”Although Pakistan eventually lost the Test by eight wickets.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mitch Marsh's Zimbabwe connection: Father Geoff Marsh's coaching stint, childhood memories and a dream of playing for Zimbabwe
articles.summary: Cricket News: Mitch Marsh will play his 100th ODI for Australia in Zimbabwe this week, a country that has played a special role in his life and cricket journey. Mar.
articles.body: Mitch Marsh will play his 100th ODI for Australia in Zimbabwe this week, a country that has played a special role in his life and cricket journey. Marsh spent three important years of his childhood in Harare when his father Geoff Marsh was Zimbabwe's head coach. More than two decades later, he is back in the country as Australia's captain and one of the team's senior players.But for Marsh, Zimbabwe is much more than just another cricket tour.'He was a big part of my childhood'Ahead of Australia's ODI series against Zimbabwe, Marsh reunited with Farai 'Happy' Mapondera, who worked at the Marsh family's home in the Harare suburb of Highland.As a 10-year-old, Marsh would spend a lot of time with Happy and the other household workers. He even preferred eating with them rather than in the house."I spent my days with him a lot of the time," Marsh told cricket.com.au. "I refused to eat in the house – I'd go and have dinner with him. He was a big part of my childhood."Happy had come to Harare Sports Club hoping to meet Marsh, but the Australian had gone to a nearby gym. When they finally met on Monday, the two shared a long embrace.Marsh then took Happy upstairs, where his family was on a video call. His sister Melissa and mother Michelle were also part of the call."Everyone was a little bit emotional," said Mitch.The Curran brothers were part of his childhoodCricket was also a big part of Marsh's life in Harare. He spent hours at Harare Sports Club playing cricket with Tom, Ben and Sam Curran, the sons of his father's coaching assistant Kevin Curran.All three later played international cricket. Tom and Sam represented England, while Ben played for Zimbabwe. Marsh's Zimbabwe counterpart Sikandar Raza joked that he was "practically a local".Marsh admitted just how strong his connection with the country was."I actually wanted to play for Zimbabwe at one point."Instead, he will play his 100th ODI for Australia in the country that helped shape his childhood.Zimbabwe was also important to his cricket careerMarsh returned to Zimbabwe with Australia in 2014, when he was still a young player trying to establish himself at international level. He was promoted to No. 3 by captain George Bailey and responded with a six-filled 89 in an ODI against Zimbabwe in Harare. A week later, he scored 86 not out, hitting seven more sixes.Those performances helped Marsh push for a place in Australia's squad for the 2015 ODI World Cup, which Australia won.Looking back at that tour, Marsh said: "I had the opportunity to bat three in a couple of those games, which was amazing," Marsh told reporters of a series that put him on the path to winning a spot in Australia’s squad for the following year’s ODI World Cup, their 2015 triumph at home. "To be honest, it feels so long ago that it's hard to really even remember the tour. But I do know that obviously I had a couple of really good innings as a young kid, and that was a great squad to be a part of."Now Marsh wants to help Australia's young playersMarsh is now one of the senior players in the Australian team.With Australia the reigning 50-over world champions, Marsh feels he has a responsibility to help young players such as Cooper Connolly, Joel Davies and Ollie Peake enjoy their early international careers. The trio are at a similar stage to where Marsh was during Australia's last ODI tour of Zimbabwe in 2014."I think a lot of us feel that responsibility to make sure these guys really enjoy playing cricket for Australia," he said. "It goes so fast. For me to now think that I'm a senior player within this group – I just want to create the best environment for them to learn, to hopefully excel, to experience playing international cricket. We are so lucky to do what we do, to get to come to places like this, tour and be together. I hope they have a great time and a similar time to what I had."A friendship that began in ZimbabweMarsh's connection with Zimbabwe did not end when his family returned to Australia. After coming back to Perth in 2004, Marsh met Riley Pattison, a young Zimbabwean boy whose family had also moved to Australia.The two had not known each other in Zimbabwe. But they met on their first day of Year Eight at Wesley College in Perth and became close friends.That friendship has lasted ever since.Last week, after Australia arrived in Harare, the entire team and support staff visited the farm leased by Pattison's family on the outskirts of the city.As the sun set over the African landscape, Marsh would have had plenty to reflect on.Zimbabwe was where he spent his childhood, learned to love cricket and built friendships that lasted a lifetime.Now, it is the place where he will celebrate another major milestone in his Australian career: his 100th ODI.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Why no one understands his position': Ashwin has one big question about Sanju Samson’s India future
articles.summary: Cricket News: Sanju Samson’s international career has been a story of immense talent, flashes of brilliance and repeated uncertainty over his place in the Indian te.
articles.body: Sanju Samson’s international career has been a story of immense talent, flashes of brilliance and repeated uncertainty over his place in the Indian team. Even after delivering on some of the biggest stages, the wicketkeeper-batter has often found himself moving in and out of the side.That pattern has now drawn strong support from former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin, who believes Samson’s prolonged struggle for a consistent place could be taking a significant mental toll.Ashwin points to Samson’s difficult journeyAshwin feels Samson’s career has been particularly challenging because of the way opportunities have come and gone over the years. The Kerala batter made his international debut back in 2014, but has never managed to establish himself as a permanent fixture across formats. According to Ashwin, even strong performances have not always guaranteed Samson an extended run.“If you are Samson, won't you feel that you did brilliantly in the World Cup and then in Ireland all the batters struggled. Then he failed one game in England and got dropped, he must be experiencing difficult mental battles and wondering why no one understands his position. His journey hasn't been easy, considering he started in 2014,” Ashwin said.From World Cup heroics to being droppedSamson’s situation became particularly striking after his performances at the 2026 ICC Men’s T20 World Cup, where he was named Player of the Tournament.He also impressed during India’s tour of Ireland, but his run in the team soon came under pressure. After three successive failures in T20Is, Samson was left out of the playing XI for the second T20I against England in July, with young Vaibhav Sooryavanshi preferred instead.Samson returned for the final game of that series but was then omitted from India’s T20I squad for the Zimbabwe tour. His next opportunity came against Afghanistan, where he returned to the XI for the opening T20I. However, he could score only 10 runs from eight deliveries, once again leaving his position open to scrutiny.'You are never sure' where the pressure comes fromAshwin believes Samson may be caught in comparisons with Sooryavanshi, making his position even more difficult and raising questions about the mental pressure he must be experiencing."When he plays well, people give the feeling of saying, 'I told you so that time itself'. Yet, when he fails, they'll say he never plays well and is inconsistent so they put pressure on him. You are never sure if the accusation from people is about Samson failing or about Vaibhav Sooryavanshi sitting out because of him playing. You wonder how it'll feel to be Sanju Samson," Ashwin added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Cricket News: Australia batter Matt Renshaw scored his maiden ODI century on Tuesday in the first match of the three-match series against Zimbabwe at the Harare Spo.
articles.body: Australia batter Matt Renshaw scored his maiden ODI century on Tuesday in the first match of the three-match series against Zimbabwe at the Harare Sports Club.Renshaw scored 109 as Australia posted 294 in the series opener. His century was the first by an Australian against Zimbabwe since Michael Clarke scored an unbeaten 105 in 2004.Renshaw helps Australia recoverRenshaw came to the crease when Australia were in trouble at 83/3 in 13 overs after opting to bat first. The left-hander took his time and kept the scoreboard moving before stepping up the attack. He brought up his fifty off 55 balls.Renshaw continued to find the boundaries and reached his century off just 86 balls. It was the fastest ODI century by an Australian against Zimbabwe. He bettered Adam Gilchrist's previous record of 89 balls, which came in the Hobart ODI in 2004.First Australian No. 6 or lower to hit ODI ton since MaxwellRenshaw's century was also the first ODI hundred by an Australian batting at No. 6 or lower since Glenn Maxwell's unbeaten 201 against Afghanistan in the 2023 World Cup. His impressive innings ended when he was caught at deep mid-wicket off left-arm fast bowler Newman Nyamhuri.Nyamhuri completed his maiden five-wicket haul with Renshaw's wicket.Australia post 294Renshaw's 109, Cooper Connolly's 51, Oliver Peake's 30 and Mitchell Marsh's 36 were the main contributions as Australia reached 294.Earlier, Cameron Green missed the Playing XI due to shoulder soreness, while fast bowler Josh Hazlewood was rested as part of workload management.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cricket News: Bangladesh women’s captain Nigar Sultana is set to relinquish the T20I captaincy following the 2026 Asian Games, bringing an end to her leadership of .
articles.body: Bangladesh women’s captain Nigar Sultana is set to relinquish the T20I captaincy following the 2026 Asian Games, bringing an end to her leadership of the side in the shortest format.According to Cricbuzz, Nigar has already communicated her decision to the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB), with the wicketkeeper-batter formally informing the board through a letter sent from Japan on Tuesday, September 15. However, she is not walking away from leadership altogether. Nigar intends to continue captaining Bangladesh in ODIs while shifting her focus in T20Is towards her batting and wicketkeeping responsibilities.Nigar wants to focus on batting and wicketkeepingNigar took over as Bangladesh’s T20I captain in 2022 and has led the side through several significant moments in the format. After the Asian Games, she wants to reduce her leadership responsibilities in T20Is to concentrate more on her individual contributions with the bat and behind the stumps.A decade-defining World Cup victoryOne of the standout moments of Nigar’s T20I captaincy came during the 2024 T20 World Cup, when Bangladesh defeated Scotland to secure their first victory at the tournament in 10 years. Nigar also played a key role as an individual during that campaign. She scored 104 runs across four innings and contributed seven dismissals as wicketkeeper, underlining her importance to the side in both departments.While Nigar enjoyed some notable successes as captain, her tenure has also faced difficult periods. Bangladesh went unbeaten to win the 2026 T20 World Cup qualifiers, strengthening their hopes ahead of the main tournament. However, their subsequent results were less convincing.They suffered a 2-1 home series defeat to Sri Lanka, while their campaign in the Scotland-Netherlands tri-series produced mixed results. At the 2026 T20 World Cup, Bangladesh managed only two victories from five matches, with those results putting Nigar’s leadership under greater scrutiny.Asian Games to mark end of T20I captaincyNigar will now lead Bangladesh in the T20 format for one final assignment at the Asian Games before stepping aside. Her decision allows Bangladesh to begin planning for a new T20I captain while retaining Nigar’s experience and leadership in ODIs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

England won the opening Test by an innings and 103 runs before securing a 194-run victory at Lord’s to seal the series. The third Test at Edgbaston saw Pakistan show greater fight, particularly in their second innings, when Shan Masood, Babar Azam and debutant Razaullah helped them recover from a disastrous start. articles.body: Laura Wolvaardt produced a record-breaking batting masterclass to guide South Africa to another emphatic victory over Zimbabwe, but the Proteas captain’s stunning century also created a major milestone in women’s international cricket.Wolvaardt smashed an unbeaten 126 off just 62 balls in the third T20I, taking her tally to 18 international centuries and putting her level with India star Smriti Mandhana at the top of the women’s international century list.Wolvaardt matches Mandhana with blistering hundredThe South African skipper was in complete control from the outset, reaching her fourth T20I century with an extraordinary strike rate of 203.22. Her unbeaten 126 featured 16 fours and four sixes, as she tore apart the Zimbabwe bowling attack and propelled South Africa to 200/1.The century was Wolvaardt’s 18th across international cricket, allowing her to join Mandhana at the summit of the women's century chart. At just 27, Wolvaardt now has another major statistical milestone in her sights, with the battle between two of the modern era's premier women's batters becoming increasingly fascinating.South African record falls tooWolvaardt’s innings was not only significant because of the international record. The 27-year-old surpassed her previous best T20I score of 115 not out, which she had made against Ireland in December last year.She also broke the South African women’s record for the highest individual T20I score, going past Shandre Fritz’s unbeaten 116 against the Netherlands in 2010. It was therefore a night of multiple milestones for the Proteas captain, who was named Player of the Match for her extraordinary effort.Meso provides support as South Africa post 200Wolvaardt found an able partner in wicketkeeper-batter Karabo Meso, who remained unbeaten on 50 from 51 balls. articles.title: Sanju Samson's  57 off 22 establishes his role of the preferred opener as India beat Afghanistan by seven-wickets to seal T20I series
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: It's not easy being Sanju Samson. He has been forever walking the line in his 10-year-old international career, partly because of team dyna.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: It's not easy being Sanju Samson. He has been forever walking the line in his 10-year-old international career, partly because of team dynamics and mostly because of his unignorable inconsistency. As he has often done in his career when pushed to a corner, he served a reminder on Tuesday night in the second T20I against Afghanistan why it's difficult to dismiss his potential in T20 cricket.In a matter of seven overs, after the Indian bowlers expectedly restricted Afghanistan to a modest 159/8 on evidently sluggish pitch, Samson buried the ghosts of the Ireland and England tour with 57 off 22 balls in a cold and merciless spell of ball-striking. In doing so, he virtually killed the game, setting the stage for Ishan to ease to an unbeaten 38 off 23 balls for India to canter to a series victory with a seven-wicket win in 14.5 overs.In the first two T20Is, India's two preferred T20I openers Abhishek Sharma and Samson regained their form after a lull post the victorious T20 World Cup campaign at home in March. Nitish Kumar Reddy bowling three overs for 3/24 would settle a few nerves in the team management which is fretting over zeroing on a seam-bowling allrounder in the white-ball format.With no major T20I assignment, barring the Asian Games later this month, lined up before 2028, this series bore very little significance. Yet, it was a series that could have determined Samson's international future. This was a banana peel series for him. He couldn't afford to have slipped here, certainly not when there is an eagerness to give 16-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi a long run. He was done in by his inconsistency in the UK two months ago where he failed to get started in four T20Is he played, forcing the team management to hand Sooryavanshi an international debut.Samson's poker face and unassuming demanour at the crease, doesn't give away his destructive ability with the willow in hand. With each of his four sixes and seven boundaries, he went about demolishing Afghanistan's spin-bowling strength in the Powerplay and dismissing doubts over his capability as a T20 batter in Indian conditions.As Samson played the dominant hand in the 88-run opening partnership in 6.2 overs before Abhishek holed out at deep mid-wicket off Sanju Samson for 39 off 19, the duo reminded the world of the treachery they could inflict on bowling attacks up front in the innings.The pitch here doesn't resemble the hard and flat concrete-like decks India played in India during the T20 World Cup. This one is tired after hosting incessant cricket for nearly a year. Afghanistan's spin attack of Mohammed Nabi, Rashid Khan, Mujeeb Ur Rahman and Noor Ahmad have fetched premium value in T20 leagues around the globe with their unconventional style of bowling. Afghanistan, trailing in the three-match series, didn't leave anything to chance and unleashed their most lethal weapons together up front in the second innings. The pitch did show signs of holding up and taking considerable turn in the latter half of the chase, but Samson decided to eliminate the threat before holing out to Rashid centimeters from the long-off boundary.Now that the series is sealed, it will be interesting see if India give Sooryavanshi another hit in the third T20I on Thursday. articles.title: 'We're not machines, we're not robots, outside noise does affect us': Sanju Samson
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Sanju Samson has spent years learning to live with the scrutiny that comes with playing for India. On Tuesday, after his 57 off 22 balls ag.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Sanju Samson has spent years learning to live with the scrutiny that comes with playing for India. On Tuesday, after his 57 off 22 balls against Afghanistan in the second T20I, he admitted that the noise from outside does get through — even if his preferred response is to switch it off.“I try to switch the Wi-Fi off. But sometimes the Wi-Fi gets switched on and comments become visible,” Samson said after India’s seven-wicket win. “Some senior player says something. So I think it’s very normal.”Samson’s innings, in which 52 of his 57 runs came in boundaries, came at a time when his place at the top of India’s T20I order is under scrutiny. The emergence of 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has added another layer to the competition for the two opening slots alongside Abhishek Sharma. Sooryavanshi had impressed on India’s recent tour of Zimbabwe, while Samson had been left out of that series after failing to convert his opportunities in the preceding Ireland, England series."Definitely, outside noise does affect cricketers in India,” Samson said. “But you need to be very clear about what your mindset is, how you need to prepare and what mindset you need to play with."“I think I have been mature enough and experienced enough to know how to handle it. Earlier, it used to hurt a little. I’m not a machine. We are not robots that we can say, ‘No, it doesn’t affect me.’ Definitely, it affects you,” he said.“If I paid attention to those things, I couldn’t bat like this,” Samson said. “Before hitting a shot, I would think ten times, ‘Yaar, out ho gaya toh phir Wi-Fi problem ho jayega.’ So instead, I tell myself, ‘Koi baat nahi.’”That mindset has become particularly important as Samson finds himself competing for a place with a teenager who has rapidly forced his way into the conversation. Samson, however, said he does not view Sooryavanshi as a rival within the dressing room.“I think they (Sooryavanshi and Abhishek Sharma) are competitors for the outside world, but we are a team and we are playing for a country,” he said. “We want to win the game first, and then it comes down to the other individuals.”Samson also said his experience as an IPL captain has helped him understand why difficult selection calls have to be made. He acknowledged that the management has a difficult task in choosing between players who are all performing, while stressing that individuals have to remain ready for their opportunities rather than dwell on selection decisions.“We can’t sulk or be in a negative frame of mind, thinking, ‘Yaar, mujhe nahi mila, usko kyun diya.’ Those kinds of mindsets don’t work here,” he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: County Championship: Ben Stokes makes half-century for Durham while Surrey skittled for 115 by Glamorgan - round-up
articles.summary: Ben Stokes makes fifty for Division Two champions Durham; Surrey were skittled for 115 and trail Glamorgan by 47 at close; Zak Crawley makes 68 for promotion-chasing Kent in Division Two as title-chasing Warwickshire lead Essex - County Championship round-up
articles.body:
Durham have already been crowned Division Two champions and secured promotion, but that did not stop them piling on the runs at The Riverside, with wicketkeeper Ollie Robinson (78 not out) also enjoying a good day with the bat.

In Division One, Surrey - battling for survival - reduced Glamorgan to 132 all out, but then mustered just 115 in reply as 20 wickets fell on the opening day at The Oval, with the visitors reaching 30 without loss in their second innings to lead by 47 runs at close of play.

At the top of the table, Ethan Bamber and Sam Hain ensured Warwickshire maintained their title challenge by ending the first day against Essex with a 17-run lead with one wicket in hand.

Seamer Bamber took six for 26 at Chelmsford to help skittle Essex for 134 and as wickets continued to tumble in Warwickshire's reply, Hain was unbeaten on 58 as the visitors closed on 151 for nine.

Warwickshire began the penultimate round of fixtures in third place, five points adrift of leaders Somerset and four adrift of defending champions Nottinghamshire , while conditions up and down the country favoured the bowlers.

Somerset's Lewis Gregory, Migael Pretorius and Jake Ball took three wickets each as they bowled out Yorkshire for 212 at Headingley, but the visitors then laboured to 68 for five and trailed by 144 at the close.

Nottinghamshire teetered on 150 for eight against Sussex at Hove before Brett Hutton (59 not out) and Tom Giles (32) shared a 74-run ninth-wicket stand, with the visitors set to resume on 232 for nine.

Leicestershire skipper Ian Holland claimed six for 38 as relegation rivals Hampshire were bustled out for 214 at Grace Road - Nathan Gilchrist adding four for 54 while visiting captain Ben Brown made a defiant 80 not out - before Hamza Shaikh (50no) helped the hosts reach 148 for seven in reply, 66 runs behind.

Bangladesh seamer Khaled Ahmed took five for 42 on his home debut for promotion-chasing Kent at Canterbury in Division Two, and Matt Milnes finished with four for 28 as Lancashire were bowled out for 161.

Kent opener Zak Crawley then made an unbeaten 68 to help the hosts reach 151 for seven, 10 runs behind with three wickets remaining as James Anderson and Tom Bailey took three apiece.

Promotion rivals Northamptonshire allowed Derbyshire to buck the trend as captain Wayne Madsen (151) and number eight Ben Aitchison (106) both made centuries to help the visitors reach 372 all out. Northamptonshire were 15 without loss at close and will resume 357 runs behind.

Middlesex closed on 324 for nine in Bristol against bottom side Gloucestershire .
