articles.title: England vs Sri Lanka: Harry Brook compared to Kevin Pietersen after stunning knock
articles.summary: Harry Brook hits a brutal century and draws comparisons with Kevin Pietersen as England thrash Sri Lanka by 119 runs in the first T20 in Southampton.
articles.body:
England 254-4 (20 overs): Brook 114* (49), Buttler 80 (44)

Sri Lanka 135 (19 overs): Wellalage 33 (21); Baker 3-12

Harry Brook hit a brutal century and drew comparisons with Kevin Pietersen as England thrashed Sri Lanka by 119 runs in the first T20 in Southampton.

The sensational Brook, after a summer without a Test hundred, crashed the ball to all parts in hitting 114 not out from 49 balls to power his side to 254-4.

His 10 fours and six sixes were ferocious - reminiscent of former England batter Pietersen, the newest addition to this side's backroom staff.

His intensity and running between the wickets was equally impressive.

"I don't even think the genius of KP could come close to what Harry Brook has talent-wise," said Brook's former captain and team-mate Ben Stokes, who was watching on TV.

Brook was six years old when Pietersen - a shock appointment as a mentor through to next year's World Cup - secured England the Ashes on the final day at The Oval in 2005.

He was 14, now old enough to understand, when Pietersen was controversially dumped by England after the 2013-14 Ashes defeat.

"I used to love watching him bat when I was younger," said Brook , external - then little more than a year into his international career.

"He always looked to take the attack to bowlers and put them under pressure. In that aspect, I'm quite similar."

Brook is, in many ways, the TikTok generation's Pietersen.

Pietersen invented the switch hit - a shot Brook rarely plays. Brook's version is that tumbling scoop over his and the wicketkeeper's head, a shot which was absent here.

They are most similar in the way they pick length, allowing them to pull, flat-bat or cut balls from spinners even in good areas.

Brook did so throughout his partnership with Jos Buttler, who also played superbly for his 80 from 44 balls. They put on 128 after debutant Aneurin Donald made 12.

And while Pietersen was educated in Pietermaritzburg, South Africa and Brook under the Cumbrian hills in Sedbergh, they come from the same cricketing school.

"That's the way I play," Pietersen said after one aggressive shot too many during a Test in 2009.

"I got to 97 playing that way so it obviously wasn't meant to be."

Those words could easily have come from the mouth of Brook.

Such words are why Pietersen and Brook have stirred opinion among England fans more than any other batters in the modern era.

"Is it really that hard to just sit back and admire these players for what they are, on the good days and the bad days, and stop berating them for doing things that we would never, ever, ever even think of doing because we simply aren't on their level to think that way?" Stokes added on social media.

Stokes, who backed Brook to succeed him as Test skipper, has always been a Brook fan.

Picking between Brook and Pietersen may well be pub chat one day, should Brook's career turn out as many hope.

For what it is worth, there is little to choose between their records at Brook's age of 27.

Pietersen's Test average, which ended at 47.28 after his 104 Tests, stood at 49.55 at this stage. Brook's is 53.08, though Pietersen had two more centuries.

Pietersen has the edge in one-day international cricket - an average of 47.87 and six centuries to Brook's 37.43 and three - but the Yorkshireman's second T20 century, hit on the south coast, is two more than Pietersen ever managed.

Perhaps where Brook lags behind is those iconic moments.

While Brook's Test best 317 on a road in Pakistan is a mark few can match, Pietersen's 158 at The Oval won England the 2005 Ashes in his fifth Test - the first of his four Ashes series wins.

Eighteen months later he made the same score against Australia in Adelaide against Shane Warne and Glenn McGrath.

Brook's best Ashes score remains 85. He is yet to win the urn.

Still, Brook's latest T20 display showed the company he could one day keep. A more mature batting style in whites this summer has also been noted.

Since being promoted to number three in England's T20 side at the World Cup earlier this year, Brook averages 95.20 at a strike-rate of 200.84.

He has scored 288 runs in the format since he was last dismissed.

"Harry Brook has today cemented himself as maybe the best all-format batter in the world," said former England bowler Steven Finn.

"[Australia's] Travis Head would be up there and so would [India's] Shubman Gill.

"Brook is lacking a Test century in the last year or so but he still averages 42 in that time.

"When you see the versatility of what he did today and the tempo he has played, he's a mighty special player."

Brook also has one clear advantage in any debate for the maverick position in a fantasy England XI.

Overlooked for the Test captaincy, Brook has won 18 of his past 20 T20s as England captain. Pietersen's stint as England skipper lasted only five months .

Sri Lanka's target was always likely to be beyond them but, even without Jofra Archer or Sam Curran, England ruthlessly dismissed their opponents for 135 in Southampton.

Brook oversaw young seamer Sonny Baker's best performance in an England shirt. He took 3-12 in four overs.

"I thought the performance tonight was near perfect," he said afterwards.

England want Pietersen to help them win the 50-over World Cup next year. He will do well to improve on this.

articles.title: England vs Sri Lanka: Harry Brook hits 42-ball hundred and Jos Buttler slams 80 as hosts win first T20 by 119 runs in Southampton
articles.summary: New white-ball mentor Kevin Pietersen watches on as England thrash Sri Lanka for 13th straight T20I win over their opponents; Ben Stokes says Harry Brook's sizzling ton shows he is perhaps better than KP was; England look to seal series victory in Cardiff on Thursday, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
White-ball captain Brook (114no off 49 balls) - who nailed six boundaries in one over - and predecessor in that role Buttler (80 off 49) plundered 128 from just 60 balls in partnership for England's second wicket once debutant Aneurin Donald (12 off 5) fell after slamming a six and a four amid a bright but fleeting cameo.

Brook and Buttler had combined for a riotous stand of 233 from 103 balls at the same venue in July as England romped to a total of 257-3 against India that secured a 4-0 series sweep, with Buttler tonking a century on that occasion and Brook an unbeaten 95.

This time around the roles were reversed with Buttler - playing his first innings since the Hundred final at Lord's on August 16 - missing out on a ton but Brook reaching three figures for the second time in T20 internationals, doing so from just 42 deliveries.

No wonder England legend Pietersen, who scored over 14,000 runs in all international cricket between 2004 and 2014, was smiling throughout in the dugout.

That expression that would surely have continued as Sri Lanka subsided to 135 all out in 19 overs in reply, to suffer a 13th successive defeat to their opponents in this format, stretching back to 2014, and England made it 21 wins from their last 24 T20Is.

The pacey, accurate and economical Sonny Baker bagged 3-12 from four overs, including bowling Kamil Mishara (10) to claim his first white-ball wicket for England, while leg-spin maestro Adil Rashid (1-31) nicked off Dasun Shanaka (24 off 14) with a peach of a delivery having just been belted for back-to-back sixes.

KP watches on as Brook dazzles at Utilita Bowl

Brook's innings was a joy to watch, with his expert ability to pick up length on full display in the 30-run fifth over of the game when he struck Sri Lankan left-arm spinner Dunith Wellalage for six boundaries in as many deliveries (three sixes, three fours).

Brook's first boundary in that set, a six onto the cushion at long-on, was a little edgy but his next five were sublime - fours over the bowler's head and down to long-on, a scooped six over fine leg, a maximum over long-off and, finally, a four behind point.

Only Phil Salt - missing this series due to a quad injury, hence why Derbyshire batter Donald has been handed a chance - has hit a faster T20I hundred for England than Brook, taking 39 balls against South Africa in 2025 when the team amassed 304-2 in Manchester.

Former England Test captain Ben Stokes took to social media to say that "I don't even think the genius of KP could come close to what Brook has talent-wise."

Stokes would later add: "Bit harsh on KP actually. Both are freak talents but Brook is better in my opinion."

Baker bags first white-ball wickets as Sri Lanka subside

Brook then rotated his bowlers smartly in the second half of the game as Sri Lanka's monumental task was made practically impossible when they started slowly and then tumbled to 69-5 inside the first 10 overs of a sorry chase, one in which Wellalage (33 off 21) top-scored, crunching four fours and two sixes.

Brook's boys - for whom seamer Jamie Overton (2-20) and spinner Liam Dawson (2-23) shared four wickets - will now hope to wrap up a series win with a game to spare in Cardiff on Thursday night (6.30pm start), ahead of the final match at Emirates Old Trafford on Saturday (2.30pm start). Both fixtures are live on Sky Sports Cricket.

Welshman Donald will be looking to make a more sustained impact in the country of his birth in the second T20 - the 29-year-old came through the Glamorgan academy and is the Cardiff county's first homegrown international since 2005 Ashes hero Simon Jones.

After Donald heaved a maximum leg-side and drilled four through extra-cover next ball, he spooned Wellalage down the ground, before watching on as Brook and Butler made mincemeat of the tourists' bowling attack - the duo spanking 28 boundaries between them.

articles.title: Is Harry Brook more talented than Kevin Pietersen? Have your say after Ben Stokes hails England white-ball captain
articles.summary: Harry Brook slams 114 not out from 49 balls - including 30 runs off one over - in England's thumping win over Sri Lanka in first T20; Sky Sports' Eoin Morgan says Brook is  producing "genius time and time again in all formats" - watch second T20 on Sky Sports on Thursday (6.30pm start)
articles.body:
Harry Brook is, in many ways, a modern-day Kevin Pietersen.

A player with jaw-dropping batting ability who can take any bowling attacking apart and make accessing any part of the ground look routine but also prone to driving fans mad with a daft dismissal.

In Southampton on Tuesday, though, we only saw the best of Brook as he tonked a 42-ball hundred - England's second-fastest in T20Is - against Sri Lanka, with his 10 fours and half a dozen sixes including six boundaries in one over off Dunith Wellalage.

The swashbuckling innings was played in front of England legend Pietersen, who has joined head coach Brendon McCullum's white-ball set-up as a mentor, up to and including the 50-over World Cup in South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe in late 2027.

And Brook's knock lured Stokes onto social media to say that, in his opinion, the Yorkshireman's ability outstrips that of Pietersen.

Stokes, on the day he struck a half-century for Durham against Worcestershire in the County Championship , wrote: "I don't even think the genius of KP could come close to what Brook has talent-wise. You are an absolute freak, Harry. You're mint to watch."

Shortly after, former Test captain Stokes added: "Bit harsh on KP actually. Both are freak talents but Brook is better in my opinion."

So, who do you think is the most talented of the two? Vote in the poll below.

Brook still has a long way to go to match Pietersen longevity-wise.

KP amassed almost 14,000 international runs between 2004 and 2014, a number he was prevented from adding to after a fallout with the ECB truncated his England career.

Brook has over 6,500 international runs since debuting in 2022, so, all being well will eclipse Pietersen's haul at some stage.

At 27, he could have over a decade left - and he hopes to use Pietersen's expertise to become even better.

Brook hopes 'hero' KP can have 'big impact' on his career

Brook said of Pietersen, after revealing he had watched highlights of his innings before Tuesday's T20: "He looked at batting slightly differently, in a similar way to me as well.

"He always wants to put the bowlers under pressure.

"He was a phenomenal player. The way he accessed different areas of the ground made it really tricky to captain and bowl to, and I'm looking forward to conversations about that.

"I mentioned to him earlier about trying to help me read surfaces and using my skills to perform on that pitch as well, not just for white-ball cricket, Test cricket as well.

"Hopefully he can have a big impact on my career. He's a hero to a lot of players. We grew up watching him and it's just awesome to have a man of his calibre in the changing room."

'Genius Brook has everything as a batter'

Brook's sizzling century against Sri Lanka was his first in any international cricket since a T20 ton versus Pakistan in February, during a World Cup match in Pallekele.

It was worth the wait. The batter's picking up of length was extraordinary in an innings highly praised by Sky Sports pundits Eoin Morgan and Kumar Sangakkara.

Sangakkara said of Brook: "He reads length so quickly. He is very light and nimble on his feet. He has oodles of time and devastating power. On the back foot against spin, he is very good at hitting over long-on, long-off, even square.

"Then against the pace there is the scoop and reverse paddle or punch down the ground for six. He has everything."

Morgan added: "I think Harry is one of our very best. It is difficult to find a player of recent generations that has Brook's ability.

"He is coming into his peak years, yet we are seeing absolute genius time and time again in all formats of the game."

Brook's last Test ton may have come over a year ago, against India at The Kia Oval, but he has knuckled down in red-ball matches of late, batting far more responsibly while notching five fifties across the summer in the international game's longest form.

In the international game's shortest form on Tuesday night, he did get a hundred - and how.

He can now chat about it with KP, a bloke he may even have more talent than…

articles.title: Ex-Pakistan batter calls India 'arrogant' as he defends Mohsin Naqvi after Asia Cup trophy row
articles.summary: Cricket News: Former Pakistan batter Mohammad Yousuf has come out in support of Asian Cricket Council (ACC) President and Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohs.
articles.body: Former Pakistan batter Mohammad Yousuf has come out in support of Asian Cricket Council (ACC) President and Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohsin Naqvi after the trophy controversy following the Women's Asia Cup final.For the second successive year, an Indian team did not collect the Asia Cup trophy after winning the tournament. Harmanpreet Kaur's side defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final to claim a record-extending eighth title, but the players stayed in the dressing room when the presentation ceremony began.The Indian team's decision came after it had made it clear that it would not accept the trophy from Naqvi, who is currently the ACC president as well as the PCB chairman.Naqvi had largely stayed away from the presentation area during the final, but was seen in the VIP box during the final over. The ceremony was subsequently delayed by around 45 to 50 minutes before eventually getting underway.Yousuf, however, defended Naqvi and accused India of displaying "arrogance" in a post on X on Tuesday.“When national pride turns into arrogance, victory brings no reward. A team may win, but a nation without humility remains a loser! No trophy, only heels on heads. #MohsinNaqvi,” Yousuf wrote on X (formerly Twitter).The latest incident mirrors what happened after last year's men's Asia Cup. India had refused to accept the trophy from Naqvi following the Pahalgam terror attack and Operation Sindoor. The men's tournament was also marked by heightened tensions between India and Pakistan, with Naqvi accused of fuelling the situation through anti-India statements on social media.India's women's team maintained a similar stance this year. Head coach Amol Muzumdar later said the BCCI had decided against accepting the trophy from Naqvi and that the players simply followed the board's position.A day later, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said India's position had been communicated to Naqvi well before the final, but the ACC president still attended the presentation ceremony.Saikia and BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla were both present at the Women's T20 Asia Cup final.When the delayed presentation finally began, only Sri Lanka came out to collect their runners-up medals. He also disclosed that the two have plans to meet for dinner.“I said good luck and best wishes, but our last conversation wasn’t only till the contract. We even spoke after that. We have planned to have dinner together sometime. I’m very fond of Rishabh. He has innocence. We will jump out of anywhere and grab you. He will play a prank or something,” he said.The decision to let Pant go came after two difficult seasons for LSG, with the franchise unable to replicate the success of its earlier campaigns. Given the enormous price tag attached to his signing, Pant's departure after just two years inevitably raised questions about the investment.There had also been speculation about friction between Goenka and Pant during their time together. At one point, tense visuals involving the two surfaced after a match, prompting comparisons with Goenka's much-discussed on-field exchange with former LSG captain KL Rahul.Goenka, however, pushed back against the perception that he is overly stern and said his relationship with Pant had always been good.Reflecting on the record purchase, he stressed that judging the value of such a deal ultimately depends on the outcome and the circumstances surrounding it.“It’s all very subjective and situation-based. When we paid ₹15 crore for Ben Stokes, it was considered expensive. Was it worth it or not? If you succeed, it pays off. If not, it doesn’t. Rishabh Pant obviously packs a punch. I have always shared a good relationship with Rishabh. People said a lot of things,” he added.After leaving LSG, Pant made his way back to his former franchise Delhi Capitals. His return came at ₹12 crore, meaning the wicketkeeper-batter took a substantial pay cut from the ₹27.4 crore that LSG had paid for him at the 2025 mega auction.LSG, meanwhile, used the opportunity to bring in India wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav as Pant's replacement in their squad.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Harry Brook scripts history, becomes first cricketer to achieve this feat in T20Is
articles.summary: Cricket News: Harry Brook has added another milestone to his remarkable run in 2026, becoming the only captain from a Full Member team to score two T20I centuries i.
articles.body: Harry Brook has added another milestone to his remarkable run in 2026, becoming the only captain from a Full Member team to score two T20I centuries in a calendar year.The England captain reached the landmark during his unbeaten 114 against Sri Lanka in the first T20I of the three-match series in Southampton on Tuesday. Brook's century came in just 42 balls, with his final score of 114 coming off 49 deliveries.Brook joins elite companyBrook's latest hundred puts him at the top of the list for most centuries as a captain in a calendar year across the three international formats for Full Member teams.Ricky Ponting holds the Test record after scoring seven centuries as captain in 2006, while Virat Kohli registered six ODI hundreds as captain in 2017 and 2018.In T20Is, Brook now stands alone with two centuries in 2026.The England skipper has also climbed into an exclusive list for most T20I centuries as captain. His two hundreds have come in just 23 innings, while Rohit Sharma and Babar Azam have three each in 62 and 78 innings respectively.Brook's stunning run continuesThe century against Sri Lanka extended a remarkable sequence for Brook. His last three T20I innings have produced scores of 79* off 35 balls against India, 95* off 45 against India and 114* off 49 against Sri Lanka.That adds up to 288 runs at an average of infinity, with a strike rate of 223.25.Brook's latest assault came after England had already made a blistering start. Jos Buttler, his predecessor as England's white-ball captain, joined him for a 128-run partnership as the hosts posted 254.Buttler smashed 80 off 44 balls, while Brook's unbeaten 114 formed the centrepiece of another dominant England batting display.England cruise to 119-run victoryEngland's batting had already put Sri Lanka under enormous pressure, and the hosts' bowlers ensured there was little chance of a comeback.Sonny Baker made an immediate impact with 3/12, while Jamie Overton claimed two wickets. Baker's pace proved particularly difficult for Sri Lanka to handle, and the visitors lost wickets regularly throughout the chase.Dunith Wellalage provided some resistance with a 33-run blitz, while Eshan Malinga added late runs, but Sri Lanka were eventually bowled out at the end of the 19th over.England completed a comprehensive 119-run victory to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.For Brook, however, the night belonged to another record, as his second T20I century of 2026 made him the only Full Member captain to achieve the feat in a calendar year.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India squad for West Indies series: Will Ravindra Jadeja make an ODI return?
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: With the majority of first-choice ODI players busy at the Asian Games and a host of players nursing injuries, it’s going to be a heady day .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With the majority of first-choice ODI players busy at the Asian Games and a host of players nursing injuries, it’s going to be a heady day for the national selectors here on Wednesday as they meet to pick the ODI team for the three-match home series against West Indies from Sept 27.TOI understands selectors are expected to spend a lot of time discussing whether they want to bring back Ravindra Jadeja, as Axar Patel will be on Asian Games duty. The other big call will be to decide on the second wicketkeeper, with KL Rahul and Hardik Pandya’s availability also a factor.It is learnt that the team management and the selectors want to move on from Jadeja. However, with Axar’s unavailability and Harsh Dubey injured, the selectors may consider Jadeja for ODIs.“Jadeja’s bowling in white-ball cricket hasn’t been up to the mark for a while now. Dubey was identified as Axar’s backup. The other spin-bowling allrounder, Washington Sundar, too will be at the Asian Games. The team management wants an established batter in the middle order,” a BCCI source told TOI.Tricky call on PandyaIn the case of Pandya, the Centre of Excellence (CoE) has shared a report which says the star allrounder should be fit for competitive cricket from Sept 20. The selectors had named him in the 50-over India ‘A’ team for the series against Australia ‘A’, which starts on Oct 6.TOI has learnt that Pandya himself doesn’t want to rush back to international cricket until he is absolutely convinced about his fitness, which will allow him to bowl 10 overs in a match. The other two seam-bowling allrounders, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Shivam Dube, too will be in Japan. It is learnt that Suryansh Shedge is also nursing an injury.Will Pant get another lifeline?TOI has learnt that the selectors are keen to give Rishabh Pant another go in the ODI format since Ishan Kishan will be at the Asian Games. Pant will be facing competition from Dhruv Jurel.“The selectors feel that Pant has the game against pace and bounce which can be useful in South Africa. He is more experienced than Jurel,” the source said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Even KP couldn’t come close’: Ben Stokes makes huge Harry Brook-Kevin Pietersen comparison
articles.summary: Cricket News: Ben Stokes has heaped praise on Harry Brook after the England white-ball captain produced another breathtaking T20I innings against Sri Lanka, even su.
articles.body: Ben Stokes has heaped praise on Harry Brook after the England white-ball captain produced another breathtaking T20I innings against Sri Lanka, even suggesting that the young batter's talent surpasses that of Kevin Pietersen.Brook smashed an unbeaten 114 off just 49 balls in the first T20I in Southampton, striking 10 fours and six sixes at a remarkable strike rate of 232.65. His assault helped England post 254/4 before they bowled Sri Lanka out for 135 in 19 overs to win by 119 runs.Stokes, who has played alongside Brook for England, took to X to express his admiration for the 27-year-old's ability.“I don’t even think the genius of KP could come close to what Harry Brook has talent-wise.“Is it really that hard to just sit back and admire these players for what they are, on the good days and the bad days, and stop berating them for doing things that we would never, ever, ever even think of doing because we simply aren’t on their level to think that way?“You are an absolute freak, Harry.“You’re mint to watch.”Stokes later followed up his post to clarify that his comparison was not intended as a slight on Pietersen.“Bit harsh on KP actually both are freak talents but Brook better IMO is my point,” he wrote.Brook's numbers at No. 3 tell the storyBrook's latest innings continued a remarkable run since he moved to No. 3 in the T20I format.The shift came after an indifferent campaign at this year's T20 World Cup, but the change in position has since brought a significant turnaround. In eight T20I innings at No. 3, Brook has accumulated 476 runs at an average of 95.20 and a strike rate of 200.84. He has two centuries and two fifties during that run.His latest hundred also saw Brook join Jos Buttler as the second Englishman to score multiple centuries in all three international formats.Brook now has two T20I centuries, 10 Test hundreds and three ODI tons. Buttler remains the other England player to achieve the feat, with two Test centuries, 11 ODI hundreds and two T20I tons.The list of players with multiple centuries across all three international formats also includes India's Rohit Sharma and KL Rahul, Pakistan's Babar Azam, West Indies great Chris Gayle, New Zealand's Brendon McCullum and Martin Guptill, and South Africa's Quinton de Kock.Brook's latest hundred was his second in T20Is. In 69 matches for England, he has now scored 1,646 runs in 60 innings at an average of 36.57 and a strike rate of 164.10, with two centuries and eight fifties.Against Sri Lanka, Brook was at the heart of another dominant England batting display. Jos Buttler provided the perfect support with 80 off 44 balls, including eight fours and three sixes, as the pair combined to power England to 254/4.Sri Lanka never came close to mounting a serious chase.Sonny Baker led England's attack with 3/12 from four overs, while Jamie Overton returned 2/20 and Liam Dawson took 2/23. Sri Lanka were eventually dismissed for 135 in the 19th over.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jos Buttler breaks Rohit Sharma's record, becomes second-highest T20I run-scorer
articles.summary: Cricket News: Jos Buttler has moved past Rohit Sharma to become the second-highest run-scorer in men's T20I cricket, adding another major milestone to his decorated.
articles.body: Jos Buttler has moved past Rohit Sharma to become the second-highest run-scorer in men's T20I cricket, adding another major milestone to his decorated international career.The England wicketkeeper-batter reached the landmark during the first T20I against Sri Lanka in Southampton on Tuesday, where the hosts cruised to a 119-run victory and took a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.Buttler came into the game needing to close the gap on Rohit's tally of 4,231 runs. He did so in style, smashing 80 off 44 balls to take his overall T20I tally to 4,292 runs from 161 matches.His innings featured eight fours and three sixes, and Buttler brought up his half-century in only 29 deliveries. He then combined with England captain Harry Brook to put Sri Lanka under severe pressure.The pair added 128 runs for the second wicket, continuing a prolific partnership after their record 233-run stand against India in England's previous T20I.Buttler eventually fell for 80, but Brook carried on to produce the defining innings of the match, hammering an unbeaten 114 off 49 balls. England finished with 254/4 from their 20 overs.Buttler moves past RohitButtler's latest knock took him to 4,292 T20I runs at an average of 34.33. His tally includes two centuries and 29 fifties.He has now moved ahead of Rohit, who finished his T20I career with 4,231 runs, and sits second on the all-time men's list.Pakistan's Babar Azam remains at the top with 4,596 runs from 145 matches at an average of 38.94.England dominate Sri LankaSri Lanka's chase never gathered momentum after England's imposing total. They managed only six runs from the opening two overs before Sonny Baker began making an impact with his pace.Baker claimed 3/12 from four overs, while Jamie Overton and Liam Dawson took two wickets each as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 135 in 19 overs.Dunith Wellalage offered some resistance with a 33-run cameo, but England remained firmly in control throughout the chase.The victory also extended England's winning run against Sri Lanka in T20Is to 13 consecutive matches.Brook was named Player of the Match after his unbeaten 114, but the night also belonged to Buttler, who moved past Rohit to claim second place on the T20I run-scoring charts.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘You are seeing a 15-year-old boy’: Sanju Samson opens up on being dropped for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: Cricket News: Sanju Samson has offered a candid take on the outside noise and his competition with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's omission from India's playing XI against A.
articles.body: Sanju Samson has offered a candid take on the outside noise and his competition with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's omission from India's playing XI against Afghanistan, insisting that competition between players cannot come at the expense of the team's larger objective.Samson and Abhishek Sharma opened in India's first two T20Is against Afghanistan, leaving Sooryavanshi on the bench despite the teenager having been named Player of the Series in Zimbabwe.While Samson managed only 10 off eight balls in the series opener, he responded emphatically in the second game, smashing 57 off just 22 deliveries as India beat Afghanistan by seven wickets to take an unassailable 2-0 lead.Speaking after the victory, Samson stressed that players must put the team's interests ahead of individual disappointment when decisions are made over the playing XI.“I think they (Sooryavanshi and Abhishek Sharma) are competitors for the outside world, but we are a team, and we are playing for a country. We want to win the game first, and then it comes down to the other individuals. We can’t sulk or be in a negative frame of mind, thinking, ‘Yaar, mujhe nahi mila, usko kyun diya.’ Those kinds of mindsets don’t work here,” Samson told reporters in the post-match press conference.Samson explains Sooryavanshi's inclusionSamson also acknowledged why Sooryavanshi was given an opportunity after his own struggles in the previous series, pointing out that selection decisions are often dictated by form and the need to win matches.“As I said before, playing for the Indian team and scoring runs is not an easy thing. You are seeing a 15-year-old boy who has come after scoring 700-800 runs. I was Player of the Tournament before that. After that, they had such a good performance, and he had to come in in some other manner,” said Samson.“I didn’t perform in two to three games, and he was in form. We wanted to win games in that series, and it was very understandable from a leadership point of view,” he added.Samson's comments came after a period in which his place in the T20I side had also been under scrutiny. After being named Player of the Tournament at the T20 World Cup, he struggled against Ireland in the first two games and played the first T20I in England before being dropped.Sooryavanshi was subsequently handed three opportunities before Samson returned for England's fifth and final T20I. Samson was then left out of India's Zimbabwe series, where Sooryavanshi made the most of his chance by scoring 151 runs in three matches and claiming the Player of the Series award.'I try to switch the Wi-Fi off'The India opener also revealed how he tries to keep external opinions from influencing him, joking that he attempts to disconnect from the constant discussion surrounding team selection.“I try to switch the Wi-Fi off. But sometimes the Wi-Fi gets switched on, and comments become visible. Some senior player says something. So I think it’s very normal.”“Definitely, outside noise does affect cricketers in India. But you need to be very clear about your mindset, how you need to prepare, and the mindset you need to play with,” he added.Samson admitted that criticism and selection debates can still affect players, but said experience has helped him deal with the pressure better.“I think I have been mature enough and experienced enough to know how to handle it. Earlier, it used to hurt a little. I’m not a machine. We are not robots, that we can say, ‘No, it doesn’t affect me.’ Definitely, it affects you,” said Samson.“If I paid attention to those things, I couldn’t bat like this. Before hitting a shot, I would think ten times, ‘Yaar, out ho gaya toh phir Wi-Fi problem ho jayega.’ So instead, I tell myself, ‘Koi baat nahi',” he added.Samson leads India to series winSamson's 57 was his first T20I half-century since the T20 World Cup final, where he was named Player of the Tournament.He smashed four sixes and seven fours against Afghanistan, while Abhishek contributed 39 off 19 balls. The pair raced to 88 from just 38 deliveries before India completed the chase with 163/3 in 14.5 overs.Earlier, Nitish Reddy's 3/24 helped restrict Afghanistan to 159/8. India won by seven wickets for the second successive game at the same venue, taking a 2-0 lead with one match remaining.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: MUMBAI: The Women's Premier League-2027 auction is likely to be conducted on October 29 in Kochi, TOI has learnt.The option of staging WPL 2027 matches in Varanasi, provided the stadium is ready by January next year, was discussed at Tuesday's WPL Governing Council meeting, which was held virtually."It has been decided that Mumbai's Brabourne Stadium will stage WPL-2027 matches. The second city for staging the WPL will be either Vadodara (Kotambi Stadium) or the new stadium in Varanasi. The BCCI is exploring the possibility of staging matches at Varanasi right now. A BCCI cricket operations team will conduct a recce of the Varanasi stadium, and assess whether it is ready or not to stage the tournament. Since it’s a new venue, we also need to conduct a few domestic/practice matches as well there," a source tracking developments told TOI on Wednesday.“The possibility of hosting WPL matches at the Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru was also discussed, but then it requires quite a few permissions from the local authorities,” the source informed.The historic Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India and the Kotambi Stadium in Vadodara will also stage the inaugural edition of the six-team ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027, with matches scheduled between Feb 14 and 28, 2027.In the past, the Brabourne Stadium has staged two WPL finals, in 2023 (inaugural season) and 2025, and missed out last year because new floodlights are being installed at the venue.The Brabourne Stadium is also the home venue of the Railways in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy, and will stage three of their ties in the upcoming season.Vadodara staged the 2026 WPL final, in which the Smriti Mandhana-captained Royal Challengers Bengaluru beat Delhi Capitals by six wickets to lift the trophy.Decision on Impact Player rule deferred to next monthMeanwhile, at a meeting of the BCCI's IPL Governing Council on Tuesday, a decision on the controversial Impact Player rule in the IPL has been deferred to a meeting of the IPL GC next month."All the franchisees have submitted their feedback on the rule. articles.title: IPL 2027: BCCI decides to stage mini-auction in India; impact player verdict awaited
articles.summary: IPL 2027 auction to be held in India as BCCI ends overseas run after franchise feedback. Decision on Impact Player rule deferred to next GC meeting in a mont...
articles.body:
The BCCI has decided to hold the IPL 2027 mini-auction in India, moving away from recent overseas hosting trends in Dubai, Jeddah and Abu Dhabi.

Venue selection will depend on hotel availability during India's wedding season from October to December, with over 100 rooms needed for franchises.

The Impact Player rule decision remains unresolved, with another Governing Council meeting expected in a month to finalise its future.

No more overseas trips! BCCI decides to bring IPL 2027 auction back to India as impact player call deferred

The BCCI has reportedly settled on bringing the IPL 2027 mini-auction back home to India, by moving away from the overseas trend that's defined the last few years.

According to Cricbuzz , this call came out of Tuesday's IPL Governing Council meeting on September 15, which is one of the biggest takeaways from that sit-down.

Ever since the 2023 auction wrapped up in Kochi, the franchises have found themselves flying out for these events, with Dubai, Jeddah and Abu Dhabi all taking turns as hosts. That pattern breaks this year, though, as the board has chosen an Indian venue for what will be a mini-auction rather than a full-scale one. However, the bigger mega auction slated for next year might still end up overseas.

Franchises had voiced their concerns about the headaches of shipping their entire delegations abroad just for a smaller mini-auction, and this decision seems to reflect that pushback.

The BCCI reportedly took stock of these complaints, especially after last year's Abu Dhabi edition left several teams grumbling about logistics and costs. With that feedback in mind, the Governing Council has now agreed to look at Indian cities as potential hosts for this year's event.

IPL 2027 mini-auction venue: Wedding season and hotel availability to shape choice

BCCI hasn't yet narrowed down on the city. As always, it comes down to whether there's enough hotel space to house all the franchises and their teams comfortably.

This year throws in an extra wrinkle as wedding season runs from October through December across India, which tends to gobble up premium hotel inventory fast. So the final venue will hinge largely on which city can guarantee five-star accommodation during that busy stretch.

The BCCI's requirement isn't small either: over 100 rooms need to be blocked for at least a couple of nights to pull this off.

IPL 2027 Impact Player decision pushed to next meeting

On another front, the fate of the Impact Player rule remains up in the air for now. The Governing Council didn't reach a verdict on it during Tuesday's meeting, and instead chose to revisit the topic at another sit-down scheduled roughly a month from now.

Interestingly, even though the majority of franchises reportedly aren't fans of the rule, many seem to think scrapping it now would be premature. Several teams have pointed out that their squad-building this season was done with the Impact Player rule firmly in mind, and the omission would put others at an advantage.

Their argument boils down to timing, as any call to ditch it should wait until the next mega auction rather than disrupting things midstream.

articles.title: 'Don't make changes': Yuvraj Singh's warning to Gautam Gambhir and management ahead of 2027 World Cup
articles.summary: Cricket News: India's preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup have already brought one major question into focus: what will their squad look like when the tournamen.
articles.body: India's preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup have already brought one major question into focus: what will their squad look like when the tournament gets underway in October?The World Cup will be staged in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, with India aiming to win the title for the third time after falling short in the 2023 final. With Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli having retired from the other formats of international cricket, their availability for the 50-over showpiece remains a key talking point.Amid the uncertainty, India's 2011 World Cup hero Yuvraj Singh has stressed the importance of one thing above all else: consistency.Speaking to Cricinfo, Yuvraj said India should settle on a core group of 16 to 20 players and give them regular opportunities in the limited number of ODIs available before the World Cup."They need to focus on building the same team to play in a year's time, because you don't want to make big changes at the last moment," Yuvraj Singh said.The former all-rounder believes regular game time will be particularly important with the ODI calendar becoming increasingly limited compared to T20 cricket."Whoever your players are, whether they are 16 or 20, it's important that everybody gets game time because obviously now there are more T20S and less 50-over cricket. Whatever matches there are, it's important that players get enough game time to prepare for the World Cup," he added.Yuvraj Singh warns against last-minute changesYuvraj pointed to India's past struggles at major tournaments and argued that sudden changes close to a World Cup can disrupt a team's preparations."Every time India has faltered is when they've made some massive changes at the last moment or in the tournament. So I think it's important that we stick to a team that we believe can lift the 2027 World Cup and stick by those guys whether they fail or succeed till that moment. Belief in the squad is very important," Yuvraj further said.He also cited India's success in the 2024 and 2026 T20 World Cups as an example of how developing a settled group can help a team prepare for a major tournament. India also reached the 50-over World Cup final in 2023."That's something that we have also done in the last two T20 World Cups," Yuvraj said. "We also played the 50-over World Cup final [in 2023]. So we have had a lot of consistency in white-ball cricket. And that's what they need to do as well, to think of first qualifying for the semis and then going on to play in the last two [knockout matches]. I think that's a long way ahead. Focus should be on getting a squad ready, which is together and ready to fight in any situation," the star former all-rounder further went on to say.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: India’s impressive run in the ongoing T20I series against Afghanistan has translated into significant gains in the latest ICC rankings, with Abhishek Sharma climbing to second place among batters and Varun Chakravarthy breaking into the top five among bowlers.The defending T20 World Cup champions have secured an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series in Delhi, with several players making their mark across the first two matches. articles.title: IPL chairman Arun Dhumal confirms push to bring 2027 auction back to India
articles.summary: Cricket News: The IPL could witness two significant developments ahead of the 2027 season, with the player auction likely to return to India after three years overs.
articles.body: The IPL could witness two significant developments ahead of the 2027 season, with the player auction likely to return to India after three years overseas and the future of the Impact Player rule back under discussion. IPL chairman Arun Dhumal has expressed his desire to bring the auction back home, while the BCCI is seeking fresh feedback from franchises and other stakeholders on the controversial substitution rule.The auction for the 2027 season is expected to be a smaller event, with the host city yet to be finalised. The previous three editions were held outside India, in Dubai, Jeddah and Abu Dhabi. Dhumal, who is set to be re-elected as IPL chairman at the BCCI Annual General Meeting on September 18, said the league would make another attempt to host the auction in India.IPL 2027 auction: BCCI keen to bring event back to IndiaThe IPL auction has been held overseas for the past three years, with Dubai hosting the 2024 auction, Jeddah staging the 2025 mega auction and Abu Dhabi hosting the 2026 auction. Dhumal said the league had been trying to bring the event back to India but faced difficulties in securing a suitable venue due to the busy wedding season."Every year we try for this to happen in India, but we don't get the venue given the heavy marriage season. So, we definitely want it to be here this year, given that it would be a smaller auction and hopefully we will get the venue," Dhumal told PTI.The host city for the auction will be decided based on the availability of the BCCI's preferred venue.Impact Player rule back under discussion ahead of IPL 2027The future of the Impact Player rule has also emerged as a key talking point ahead of the 2027 season, with the BCCI seeking fresh feedback from franchises. The matter was discussed at a recent IPL Governing Council meeting after the board approached teams for their views on the rule, which is currently scheduled to remain in place until 2027.Several prominent Indian cricketers, including Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill, former India captain Rohit Sharma, Hardik Pandya and Axar Patel, have expressed reservations about the rule. One of the key concerns raised by players is that it reduces the importance of all-rounders by allowing teams to bring in a specialist batter or bowler during a match.Ahead of IPL 2026, several captains had conveyed their concerns to the BCCI, renewing calls for the rule to be scrapped. Dhumal said the board was open to reviewing the concept but would consult all stakeholders before making a decision."The matter is under discussion. Will take a feedback from all the stakeholders and then take a call on this," he said.The Impact Player rule allows teams to substitute a player at any stage of a match, giving them the flexibility to bring in an additional batter or bowler depending on the match situation.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
